questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q01

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q01 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Source set: A student is researching whether pre-order lunch forms can reduce unwanted trays. Which research question is most focused for this inquiry?\

answer.text: A. What is the history of every school lunch program?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too broad for the inquiry.

answer.text: B. How can student pre-order lunch forms help reduce unwanted trays?

feedback.text: Correct. This question is specific, researchable, and aligned to the unit inquiry.

answer.text: C. Why do all students like different foods?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is broad and not focused on unwanted trays.

answer.text: D. Are forms always good or always bad?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is absolute and not research-focused.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q02

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q02 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Source: A district pilot report includes before-and-after tray data from a pre-order lunch program. Why is this source useful?\

answer.text: A. It has a formal title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title alone does not prove usefulness.

answer.text: B. It is long.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not prove relevance or reliability.

answer.text: C. It mentions school in general.

feedback.text: Incorrect. General school information is not enough.

answer.text: D. It provides evidence directly related to the research question.

feedback.text: Correct. The source gives data about the exact topic being researched.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q03

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q03 [MLA.ENG2.R.10] Original: "Reminders helped more students complete the pre-order form after the first week." Which paraphrase is accurate?\

answer.text: A. After the first week, reminders increased student completion of the pre-order form.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately restates the source in new wording.

answer.text: B. Reminders made the form unnecessary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This changes the meaning.

answer.text: C. Students completed no forms after reminders.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contradicts the source.

answer.text: D. The form was removed after one week.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not stated.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q04

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q04 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which note best records source information without copying too much?\

answer.text: A. "The report says the thing was good."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: B. "All waste ended forever."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overstates the source.

answer.text: C. Pilot report: fewer unwanted trays after meals were prepared from student selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This note is concise and accurate.

answer.text: D. "Lunch exists."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not useful research information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q05

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q05 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which sentence best integrates source evidence?\

answer.text: A. A district pilot report found fewer unwanted trays after staff prepared meals from student pre-order selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This clearly identifies the source and finding.

answer.text: B. The report said stuff happened.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: C. Trays and forms were a thing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and unclear.

answer.text: D. Everyone knows forms are good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unsupported.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q06

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q06 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which sentence best explains why the evidence matters?\

answer.text: A. Evidence is always evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain this evidence.

answer.text: B. A source has information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

answer.text: C. Reports are written by people.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain relevance.

answer.text: D. The finding matters because student selections helped staff prepare meals students were more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains the connection between evidence and purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q07

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q07 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Which revision best fits a student audience?\

answer.text: A. Pre-order compliance creates operational efficiency.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too formal for students.

answer.text: B. Completing the form helps the cafeteria prepare meals students are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Correct. This is clear and audience-aware.

answer.text: C. The thing helps lunch stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

answer.text: D. Food systems must optimize outputs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q08

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q08 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which visual best supports the research finding?\

answer.text: A. A random hallway photo.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It does not connect to the evidence.

answer.text: B. A decorative background only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration alone does not explain evidence.

answer.text: C. A labeled before-and-after chart showing unwanted trays before and after the pilot.

feedback.text: Correct. This visual directly supports the source finding.

answer.text: D. A picture of unrelated school supplies.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This visual is unrelated.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q09

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q09 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which source would be least useful for the research question about pre-order forms and unwanted trays?\

answer.text: A. A cafeteria manager interview about form completion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is relevant to the process.

answer.text: B. A pilot report with tray data.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is directly relevant.

answer.text: C. A student feedback summary about understanding the form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is relevant to audience communication.

answer.text: D. A blog post about unrelated sports uniforms.

feedback.text: Correct. This source does not address lunch forms or unwanted trays.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q10

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q10 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which transition best adds a related source finding?\

answer.text: A. In addition

feedback.text: Correct. This transition adds related information.

answer.text: B. However

feedback.text: Incorrect. This usually signals contrast.

answer.text: C. Instead

feedback.text: Incorrect. This signals replacement.

answer.text: D. Although

feedback.text: Incorrect. This introduces contrast or qualification.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q11

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q11 [MLA.ENG2.L.01] Which sentence is complete and clear?\

answer.text: A. Because the source shows fewer trays.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment.

answer.text: B. Source trays fewer students because.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear.

answer.text: C. The source shows fewer unwanted trays after the pre-order pilot.

feedback.text: Correct. This is complete and clear.

answer.text: D. When the form and chart.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is incomplete.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q12

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q12 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which presentation plan best shows collaboration?\

answer.text: A. One person speaks while the team ignores the source.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show shared, source-based work.

answer.text: B. One member explains the evidence, one explains the synthesis, one explains the visual, and one explains the revision choices.

feedback.text: Correct. This plan shows purposeful collaboration.

answer.text: C. Everyone repeats the same unsupported opinion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is repetitive and not evidence-based.

answer.text: D. The team skips the visual explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs the publication choices explained.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q13

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q13 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which synthesis best combines Source A and Source B? Source A: The pilot report found fewer unwanted trays. Source B: Reminders helped more students complete the form.\

answer.text: A. The pilot reduced unwanted trays, and reminders supported the process by helping more students complete the form.

feedback.text: Correct. This accurately combines both source ideas.

answer.text: B. The sources are both about school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

answer.text: C. Reminders proved the report was false.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not match the source information.

answer.text: D. The pilot had no connection to forms.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contradicts the source set.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q14

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q14 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Which sentence should be revised because it is not audience-aware?\

answer.text: A. Completing the form helps staff prepare meals students are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is student-friendly.

answer.text: B. The chart shows fewer unwanted trays after the pilot.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is clear.

answer.text: C. A reminder can help students complete the form on time.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is clear and relevant.

answer.text: D. Stakeholders must enact compliance with food-service optimization protocols.

feedback.text: Correct. This wording is too formal and unclear for students.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q15

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q15 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which publication choice best matches Unit 4 standards?\

answer.text: A. A copied report with no audience revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The product should be adapted for its audience.

answer.text: B. A poster with no source evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The product must be source-based.

answer.text: C. A student-facing flyer with accurate evidence, clear explanation, and a labeled visual.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches source-based writing and collaborative multimedia publication.

answer.text: D. A private note with no publication plan.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The unit includes publication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q16

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q16 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which sentence overstates the evidence?\

answer.text: A. The pilot report found fewer unwanted trays.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is measured and accurate.

answer.text: B. Pre-order forms will eliminate all cafeteria waste forever.

feedback.text: Correct. This claims more than the evidence proves.

answer.text: C. Reminders helped more students complete the form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This accurately states the source finding.

answer.text: D. A chart can help students understand the change.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is reasonable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q17

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q17 [MLA.ENG2.R.10] Which paraphrase keeps the meaning of this source detail: "Students understood the purpose better when the message used simple wording and a labeled chart"?\

answer.text: A. Students did not need any message.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This contradicts the source detail.

answer.text: B. A chart made all problems disappear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overstates the source.

answer.text: C. Simple wording and a labeled chart helped students understand why the form mattered.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the meaning accurately.

answer.text: D. Students only cared about colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not stated.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q18

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q18 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which sentence has the most appropriate academic voice?\

answer.text: A. The pre-order process helped staff prepare meals based on student selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This is precise and evidence-based.

answer.text: B. The lunch form was super awesome.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and exaggerated.

answer.text: C. The report said stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: D. Students should do the thing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q19

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q19 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Chart data: Before the lunch pre-order pilot, students left 42 unwanted trays. After the pilot, students left 18 unwanted trays. Which caption best supports this before-and-after chart?\

answer.text: A. This chart is colorful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the evidence.

answer.text: B. The chart shows unwanted trays decreased from 42 before the pilot to 18 after the pilot.

feedback.text: Correct. This caption explains the before-and-after data shown in the chart.

answer.text: C. A chart appears here.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague.

answer.text: D. Charts are useful sometimes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is general and unsupported.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q20

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q20 [MLA.ENG2.L.01] Which revision fixes the fragment: "Although some students needed reminders."\

answer.text: A. Although some students needed reminders and.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is still incomplete.

answer.text: B. Some although students reminders.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unclear.

answer.text: C. Although reminders.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is still a fragment.

answer.text: D. Although some students needed reminders, form completion improved after the first week.

feedback.text: Correct. This creates a complete sentence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q21

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q21 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Which detail best supports the idea that communication affects form completion?\

answer.text: A. Student feedback said simple wording and a labeled chart helped students understand the form's purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. This source detail connects communication choices to student understanding.

answer.text: B. The cafeteria has tables.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not address communication or form completion.

answer.text: C. The school has hallways.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is unrelated.

answer.text: D. Students take several classes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not support the idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q22

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q22 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Which question should guide final revision?\

answer.text: A. Can I make the wording harder so it sounds advanced?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision should improve clarity.

answer.text: B. Can I remove the evidence to shorten the product?

feedback.text: Incorrect. The communication must remain source-based.

answer.text: C. Will the intended audience understand the evidence, explanation, visual, and action step?

feedback.text: Correct. This checks audience awareness and publication readiness.

answer.text: D. Can I use a random visual to fill space?

feedback.text: Incorrect. Visuals should support meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q23

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q23 [MLA.ENG2.C.01] Which oral explanation best supports the publication plan?\

answer.text: A. We picked the chart because it looked nice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain how the visual supports evidence.

answer.text: B. We did not use the sources.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The publication must be source-based.

answer.text: C. We made the words complicated so adults would notice.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience is students.

answer.text: D. We used a labeled chart because it shows the change in unwanted trays and helps students understand the evidence quickly.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects visual choice, evidence, and audience needs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q24

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q24 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which sentence best combines evidence, explanation, and audience purpose?\

answer.text: A. The report is about lunch and students should care.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague.

answer.text: B. The pilot report found fewer unwanted trays after staff used student selections, so students should complete the form to help the cafeteria prepare meals they are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Correct. This integrates evidence, explains why it matters, and gives an audience-focused action.

answer.text: C. Lunch forms are a thing at school.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general.

answer.text: D. The chart is nice and the form exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q25

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q25 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which final checklist best represents the Unit 4 workflow?\

answer.text: A. Research question, reliable source, accurate paraphrase, synthesis, expository explanation, audience revision, and purposeful visual.

feedback.text: Correct. This checklist follows the full research-to-publication process.

answer.text: B. Random topic, copied source, no explanation, unrelated visual.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not match Unit 4 standards.

answer.text: C. Opinion only, no source check, no revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unit 4 requires source-based communication.

answer.text: D. Difficult words, hidden evidence, and decoration only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Clarity, evidence, and audience fit are required.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q26

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q26 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Topic: school gardens. Which research question has the best scope for one assignment?\

answer.text: A. Are gardens good?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too broad and mostly opinion-based.

answer.text: B. What is a plant?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too narrow and asks for a simple definition.

answer.text: C. How could a school garden support science learning for tenth-grade students during one semester?

feedback.text: Correct. This question is focused by topic, audience, subject area, and time frame.

answer.text: D. Why should everyone love gardens forever?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This wording is biased and too broad.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q27

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q27 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] A student asks, "What about recycling?" What is the main problem with this research question?\

answer.text: A. It is too narrow because it can be answered with one fact.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The problem is not that it is too narrow.

answer.text: B. It is only a vague topic, not a focused research question.

feedback.text: Correct. It does not ask what the student wants to learn about recycling.

answer.text: C. It is already fully refined.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It needs a focus, audience, place, or effect.

answer.text: D. It includes too much evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It includes no evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q28

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q28 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Broad topic: cafeteria food waste. Which revision narrows the topic by solution and time frame?\

answer.text: A. How could a pre-order lunch form reduce cafeteria food waste during one semester?

feedback.text: Correct. This question names a solution and time frame.

answer.text: B. Is food waste bad?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is broad and opinion-based.

answer.text: C. What is food?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too narrow and asks for a definition.

answer.text: D. Why is lunch the best class?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a researchable academic question.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q29

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q29 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Research Question: How could a school garden support science learning? Source A: A state university agriculture extension article by a science education specialist explains classroom garden observations and was updated in 2025. Why is Source A reliable?\

answer.text: A. It gives no author or evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The source includes an author role and relevant examples.

answer.text: B. It is an advertisement for tools.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The source is a university extension article, not an ad.

answer.text: C. It uses insults instead of evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. No loaded insult is described.

answer.text: D. It is current, relevant, and written by a knowledgeable specialist.

feedback.text: Correct. These features support reliability and credibility.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q30

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q30 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Source B says, "Only foolish schools avoid gardens." What does this wording show?\

answer.text: A. Loaded language that suggests bias.

feedback.text: Correct. "Only foolish schools" attacks one side instead of providing evidence.

answer.text: B. Neutral academic tone.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The wording is not neutral.

answer.text: C. Current data from a study.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The sentence gives no data.

answer.text: D. A valid measurement method.

feedback.text: Incorrect. No method is described.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q31

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q31 [MLA.ENG2.RS.01] Research Question: How could a school garden support science learning? Source A says gardens let students observe plant growth, soil conditions, and ecosystem relationships. Which note is most useful?\

answer.text: A. Gardens are outside.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is true but too general to answer the research question.

answer.text: B. Students are people.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not help answer the research question.

answer.text: C. Gardens can support observations of plant growth, soil, and ecosystems.

feedback.text: Correct. This note is brief, accurate, and relevant to the research question.

answer.text: D. The source has words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not useful source information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q32

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q32 [MLA.ENG2.R.10] Original: Garden journals can help students record observations and connect evidence to science vocabulary. Which paraphrase is accurate?\

answer.text: A. Journals make science unnecessary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The original says journals support science work.

answer.text: B. Garden journals are always perfect.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The original does not make that absolute claim.

answer.text: C. Students should never write observations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The original says journals help students record observations.

answer.text: D. Students can use garden journals to track what they see and explain it with science terms.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning in new wording.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q33

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q33 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Findings: A pre-order lunch pilot reduced unwanted trays. Student reminders helped more students complete forms. Which organization pattern fits best?\

answer.text: A. Chronological story plot

feedback.text: Incorrect. The goal is to explain research findings, not narrate a story.

answer.text: B. Cause and effect

feedback.text: Correct. The paragraph should explain how the form and reminders led to reduced waste.

answer.text: C. Random list

feedback.text: Incorrect. Research findings need logical organization.

answer.text: D. Definition only

feedback.text: Incorrect. The findings explain an effect, not only a definition.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q34

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q34 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which sentence uses the best academic voice?\

answer.text: A. Lunch forms are super awesome and fixed everything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and exaggerated.

answer.text: B. Everybody should just do lunch forms because I said so.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and unsupported.

answer.text: C. Pre-order lunch forms may reduce waste when staff prepare meals from student selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This is clear, measured, and source-based.

answer.text: D. Forms are, like, the best thing ever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and biased.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q35

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q35 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Finding: A district report found that the pre-order pilot reduced unwanted trays. Which sentence best integrates the source?\

answer.text: A. A district report found that the pre-order pilot reduced unwanted trays after staff prepared meals from student selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence identifies the source and states the finding clearly.

answer.text: B. The report had stuff about trays.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

answer.text: C. Trays went down or whatever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and unclear.

answer.text: D. The lunch thing was awesome.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is opinion, not source integration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q36

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q36 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Which transition best adds a related second source?\

answer.text: A. However

feedback.text: Incorrect. This usually signals contrast.

answer.text: B. Instead

feedback.text: Incorrect. This signals replacement or contrast.

answer.text: C. Although

feedback.text: Incorrect. This introduces contrast or qualification.

answer.text: D. In addition

feedback.text: Correct. This transition adds related information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q37

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q37 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] A student team is creating a one-page digital flyer for students about reducing unwanted lunch trays. Which choice best matches the audience and purpose?\

answer.text: A. Copy every paragraph from the report onto the flyer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A flyer for students needs selected information, not an entire report.

answer.text: B. Use a short headline, one clear research finding, and a simple visual that shows why completing the pre-order form matters.

feedback.text: Correct. This choice combines audience awareness, evidence, and multimedia design.

answer.text: C. Use only a decorative image with no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A visual must support the message and evidence.

answer.text: D. Write a long formal memo to cafeteria staff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The assigned audience is students, not cafeteria staff.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q38

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q38 [MLA.ENG2.W.04] Draft text for students: "Failure to comply with pre-order procedures results in inefficient meal allocation." Which revision is most audience-aware?\

answer.text: A. Completing the pre-order form helps staff prepare meals students are more likely to choose.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning accurate while making the message clearer for students.

answer.text: B. Students are failing the lunch system.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This blames the audience and does not improve clarity.

answer.text: C. Lunch allocation inefficiency exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is still vague and too abstract.

answer.text: D. Forms are forms, so do them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is informal and does not explain the purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q39

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q39 [MLA.ENG2.W.03] Source finding: A district pilot report found fewer unwanted trays after staff prepared meals from student pre-order selections. Which sentence is most publication-ready?\

answer.text: A. The lunch thing helped stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and informal.

answer.text: B. Forms fixed every waste problem forever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overstates the evidence.

answer.text: C. Students should just do the form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives an action but does not explain the evidence.

answer.text: D. The pilot report found fewer unwanted trays after staff prepared meals from student pre-order selections.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence is accurate, specific, and source-based.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q40

Question ID: ENG2_U04_UA_Q40 [MLA.ENG2.C.03] Which visual best supports the source-based message?\

answer.text: A. A random cafeteria photo with no label.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A visual must support the evidence.

answer.text: B. A decorative border around the title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration does not explain evidence.
